context: v0.6.0: adds intake mode (issue report -> solver models -> solution.md plan) - new intake.py, solver seats in providers.py (text mode), CLI subcommand; version bump; 9 new tests, suite 53/53

deterministic_findings.title: Possible hardcoded secret in added code
deterministic_findings.recommendation: Move the value to the secret store / environment and rotate it if it was ever real.

reviewer_reports.summary: The intake mode introduces several reliability and correctness risks: unbounded thread pool usage without per-solver timeouts, missing cooldown/dedup for solver failures, no rate-limit guard for rapid re-runs, and the provider build path does not enforce text_mode for all solver types. These can cause alert floods, hanging processes, and resource exhaustion in production.

findings.title: Thread pool with no per-solver timeout or cancellation
findings.evidence: with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=len(solvers)) as pool: ... fut.result()  # no blocking timeout; each solver runs unbounded
findings.recommendation: Add a per-solver timeout (e.g., 60s) via pool.submit(fn, timeout=60) or wrap fut.result() in a timeout guard. Without this, a hung or deadlocked solver blocks the entire intake and consumes a thread slot permanently.

findings.title: No cooldown or dedup between solver retries / re-runs
findings.evidence: run_intake iterates solvers once; there is no guard against re-running intake rapidly, no back-off, and no dedup of identical failure patterns. In production, a transient API outage could cause repeated immediate re-runs, flooding logs and consuming API quota.
findings.recommendation: Add a module-level cooldown (e.g., 60s) or a simple file-based lock that prevents re-entry within a window. Also record the last-run timestamp in intake.json and surface it in the CLI so operators can see throttle state.

findings.title: build_provider does not pass text_mode for non-gemini openai-compatible specs
findings.evidence: When kind == "openai-compatible", the call is openai_compatible(base, model, key_env, extra, system=system) — but system is only set from text_mode in the function signature default. If text_mode=True is passed, the system prompt is _SOLVER_SYSTEM, which is correct; however the code path at line 168 calls openai_compatible with system=system where system defaults to _SYSTEM if not provided, potent
findings.recommendation: Ensure that when text_mode=True is used for openai-compatible providers, the system argument is explicitly _SOLVER_SYSTEM, not relying on the default. Add an assertion or explicit branch: if text_mode: system = _SOLVER_SYSTEM

findings.title: ThreadPoolExecutor with len(solvers) workers may exhaust resources if solver count grows
findings.evidence: max_workers=len(solvers) creates a worker per solver. If a user configures many solvers (e.g., 10+), this creates 10+ concurrent threads with no upper bound beyond process limits.
findings.recommendation: Cap max_workers to a reasonable constant (e.g., 4 or 8) regardless of solver count: max_workers=min(len(solvers), 4). This prevents resource exhaustion while still allowing parallelism for the typical 2-3 solver setup.

findings.title: No test for solver timeout or failure-to-respond scenario
findings.evidence: The test suite has 9 new tests but none exercise a solver that hangs or exceeds a reasonable time limit. Without this, the timeout recommendation has no coverage and regressions would go undetected.
findings.recommendation: Add a test that provides a solver fn that time.sleep(120) or otherwise blocks, and verify that run_intake returns ok=False or times out gracefully. This guards against the unbounded thread issue.
